top.title: ‘You Call Him Out’ — Former Steelers Star Unimpressed With Mike McCarthy’s Handling of DK Metcalf’s Ejection
top.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf faced a difficult situation as he was ejected in the third quarter of the Steelers’ game against the Philadelphia Eagles, which ended in a 19-16 loss. The wide receiver was seen losing his composure as he appeared to get physical with safety Cooper DeJean. Metcalf was ejected shortly after he was seen poking DeJean in the eye. Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy seen on the sideline during the first quarter of an NFL game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Steelers Legend Criticizes McCarthy over Metcalf Ejection In a recent episode of ‘NFL on CBS’, two-time Super Bowl champion with the Steelers Bryant McFadden shared his views on the wide receiver’s ejection and how the coaching staff handled it. He said: “I didn’t like how he (McCarthy) handled it. I think we’re in a moment now where we’re starting to see this become a recurring theme for DK. You brought up something that I totally forgot about a year ago, against Detroit, when he got into a spat with a fan in the stands while the game was going on.” “I didn’t like how [Mike McCarthy] handled it.” @BMac_SportsTalk talks about DK Metcalf’s ejection and how the coaching staff dealt with it. #Scoreboard pic.twitter.com/bZJoqputNm — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 22, 2026 Metcalf’s ejection came in the third quarter. He was initially flagged for taunting and was subsequently ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct. When asked about the ejection, head coach Mike McCarthy said: “We need him (Metcalf). We need him in those games, and that’s not acceptable to get thrown out of the game,” and added, “We can’t have players getting ejected from games.” McFadden shared his point of view on the head coach’s reaction and said: “Now, Mike McCarthy was not the head coach. That was Mike T. But clearly, Mike McCarthy … you’re aware of some of these past actions by DK. At that time, that’s when you call him out in a respectful, professional way. We cannot tolerate this. These are non-negotiables.” The ejection wasn’t the only thing Metcalf caught flak for after week 11’s game as he has also been facing criticism for leaving the stadium before the reporters were let in. When asked about it on Monday, Metcalf admitted he was avoiding the media, adding to fans’ frustration. The head coach’s comments caught McFadden’s attention, as he believed that McCarthy was saying things that everyone already knew. Fans and analysts would like to know what the head coach would have told the wide receiver in a professional manner. It will be interesting to see how the head coach deals with this recurring situation involving the wide receiver, as this is Metcalf’s third ejection since entering the NFL in 2019, tying Dre Greenlaw for the most disqualifications over that span. top.title: Quiet around potential Simon Holmstrom extension talks could prove best for Islanders star after key change
top.description: Simon Holmstrom (92) of the New York Islanders reacts after scoring a goal against the Anaheim Ducks in Anaheim, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. Things have stayed quiet around a potential contract extension for Simon Holmstrom, and right now, it certainly behooves the Islanders’ winger to keep waiting rather than negotiate in-season. Not only because of the salary cap boom that keeps lifting contracts higher and higher, but also because Holmstrom’s play so far this season is reshaping his value entirely. Holmstrom has always had the potential to score a lot more than he did and to play a lot higher up in the lineup than he had. He’s finally realizing it now. Coming into Monday night’s game against the Maple Leafs, he was riding a hot streak of six goals and 11 points in his past seven games. He has been on the Islanders’ top line for over a month, and the lack of confidence he would sometimes display in that spot in years past is completely gone. “When I think back, obviously I had a lot of chances to watch last year [while out with a torn ACL]. I think this year, you see him being more in an attack mindset, even when he’s going to work,” Kyle Palmieri, who’s played alongside Holmstrom and Bo Horvat for most of this season, told The Post. “I noticed it last game [in Detroit], especially below the goal line. He’s doing it in an attack mode as opposed to, ‘Where do I pass this to?’ Simon Holmstrom (92) of the New York Islanders reacts after scoring a goal against the Anaheim Ducks in Anaheim, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. NHLI via Getty Images “He’s looking to get a step on a guy or use his long reach to carry up to the net or find a guy in the slot that’s open. I think when you look at his goal the other night, he’s putting himself in scoring areas and obviously finishing too.” The numbers and charts back up Palmieri’s eyes. Holmstrom is shooting between the dots at an exceptional rate, and all of his goals have come from there as well. He’s averaging an extra 1.21 shots and 2.07 attempts per 60 minutes this season compared to last, both career highs, and it hasn’t yet hurt his shooting percentage. Over 25 percent of the way through the season, Holmstrom is on a 38-goal, 68-point pace. A year ago, a suggestion that Holmstrom’s next contract would be worth $8 million annually would have been laughed out of the room. His age works slightly against him, as he’ll enter the 2027 campaign at age 26 without having seen any Triple-A pitching. However, this hasn’t stopped late-blooming players from becoming significant role players. Even if Briley doesn’t sustain this level of power in 2027, he should still earn a starting job on the Knights (or another Triple-A club) by the middle of the season.

That was the message the Jets delivered to their fans with Sunday’s 27-24 victory over the Chargers . A segment of Jets fans now view wins as losses because it damages the team’s draft position, but Jets players and coaches are trying to win games, not worry about next April’s draft. The Jets now are 3-8 with six games remaining. Some of those games look winnable, so the pro-tank crowd now is bracing itself for more sad Sunday nights watching their draft positioning sink. It starts this week against a Dolphins team that is starting Kyle McCord at quarterback. The Jets play the Cardinals on Dec. 20, when Arizona could be starting rookie Carson Beck or 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson under center. The next week, they face a suddenly vulnerable Patriots team that may have ex-Giants backup Tommy DeVito as its starter. The Jets finish the season in Buffalo; the Bills, who are currently 9-1, may have their playoff position wrapped up by then and could play backups. top.title: The full analysis of Chivas' commanding win over Cruz Azul
top.description: The full analysis of Chivas' commanding win over Cruz Azul Guadalajara capped off the Apertura 2026 regular season with a statement win. The 1-0 victory over Cruz Azul on Matchday 17 showcased the competitiveness, solidity and tactical versatility that have defined Gabriel Milito’s team, who made home advantage count to secure top spot and head into the playoffs full of confidence. The keys to the Red and Whites’ victory: Intensity and penetration from the start: Chivas set a high tempo from the opening minutes, pressed high and constantly looked to get in behind the Cruz Azul defense. Santiago Sandoval was central to that approach, moving across the front line, while Bryan González’s runs in behind, Richard Ledezma’s forward surges and Daniel Aguirre’s overlapping runs provided different ways to threaten. Solidity to control the game: The Rebaño once again showed why they have the best defense in the tournament. Diego Campillo delivered another top-class performance, winning his duels with Gabriel Fernández and limiting the Cruz Azul striker’s opportunities. Beyond his defensive assurance, he also contributed on the ball, including a pass that nearly led to a goal for Santiago Sandoval. Sandoval, a headache for the Cruz Azul defense: The young Chivas player stood out for his link-up play, movement and ability to receive on the turn under pressure. His first touches allowed him to beat opponents, win duels and consistently draw fouls: he was fouled six times during the match, a reflection of how difficult he was to contain. Efraín Álvarez, the star of the night: In addition to scoring the winner, the midfielder once again demonstrated his importance to the team’s overall play. He excelled in combination play, linked up with Ledezma through switches of play and nearly added an assist after a superb individual move ended with a through ball for Bryan González. His attacking impact in the closing stretch of the regular season has been significant: he was directly involved in three goals over the last three Liga MX matches, with a goal and an assist against Atlante and another goal against Cruz Azul. A meaningful victory heading into the playoffs The win carried extra significance because it came against an opponent in excellent form. Guadalajara beat Cruz Azul for the first time in ten matches and ended La Máquina’s seven-match unbeaten run, which included five wins and two draws. Chivas not only made home advantage count but also confirmed their ability to compete in every phase of the game, combining attacking quality with the defensive solidity that saw them concede the fewest goals in the Apertura 2026. Guadalajara made a statement on the final matchday and will enter the playoffs as the top seed, with a team performance that offered plenty of encouraging signs. top.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis ahead of Joshua clash
top.description: Tyson Fury will face British heavyweight rival Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month (Chanakarn LAOSARAKHAM) Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," said the heavyweight boxer. "It was like a living version of the pits of hell. "I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much. "The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London." Fury has made the revelations about his mental health in a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday. The 38-year-old is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua, a fellow former world champion, in Cardiff on December 11 -- a bout that will be broadcast live on Netflix. Fury recalled hearing the radio talking to him, and begging wife Paris to get him out of the hospital because "the Illuminati" wanted him. Following his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with alcohol and drug addiction. "It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind," he said. "I wouldn't be able to sit and have a conversation because I'd be hearing stuff in my mind. "I didn't know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again." After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed. Fury said a turning point in his life came when he was on a night out for Halloween in 2017. "I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, 'I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I'm a fat mess addicted to alcohol'," he said. But Fury added he channelled his disgust into a comeback which led him to return to training, focus more on his family and claim another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020. jdg/nf

top.title: USA joint bid and UK confirmed as 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup hosts
top.description: FIFA announced Monday that the USA will co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, while the UK will host in 2035 (OZAN KOSE) FIFA on Monday confirmed that a joint bid led by the United States will host the expanded, 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031, while the United Kingdom will host the following edition in 2035. The winning bids were waved through by acclamation after FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed the USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time. The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035. Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at a virtual gathering of FIFA's member associations. "As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years." The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final. The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams. The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times. - 'Landmark moment' - US Soccer reacted to the announcement by saying the awarding of the 2031 tournament gave the country the chance to "build on the momentum" of this year's World Cup as well as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The United States are the reigning Olympic women's football champions. No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. A joint statement by the four UK national associations described the announcement as "a landmark moment". It is not yet known which cities will host matches at the respective tournaments, but most matches in 2031 are likely to take place in the United States while England can expect to have the lion's share of venues in 2035. The UK bid proposed 22 stadiums in total, with 16 in England, three in Wales, two in Scotland and one in Northern Ireland. Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell said the two venues in the country would be the 52,000-seat Hampden Park in Glasgow as well as Hibernian's 20,000-seat Easter Road home in Edinburgh. top.description: 📹 In a dull affair, São Paulo lead, but Botafogo snatch a draw Botafogo and São Paulo drew 1-1 at the Estádio Nilton Santos on Monday (23) in Matchday 36 of the 2026 Brasileirão. The match was typical of two teams that have disappointed their fans throughout the season and have little left to play for in the closing stages of the league campaign. São Paulo opened the scoring in the first half through Pedro Lima, who finished off an assist from Luciano. Botafogo, meanwhile, showed little ability to put their opponents under pressure. The equalizer finally came late in the match, with Tiquinho Soares pouncing on a rebound off the goalkeeper. In stoppage time, Marçal (Botafogo) was sent off for elbowing an opponent, sparking a brief scuffle on the pitch that also resulted in a red card for Wendell (São Paulo). 🚦 Where things stand The result left São Paulo in 11th place with 45 points, safe from relegation but also out of contention for a return to the Libertadores. Botafogo, meanwhile, remained in 14th with 43 points—just three ahead of Corinthians, who occupy the first relegation spot and have yet to play this round. Botafogo will look to secure their top-flight survival against Bahia at the Nilton Santos next Saturday (28), and against Santos at Vila Belmiro on December 2. São Paulo, meanwhile, will wrap up their 2026 Brasileirão campaign against Remo at MorumBIS next Thursday (26), and against Athletico-PR at the Arena da Baixada on December 2. top.title: Huskies start fast, can’t hold on in Maui Invitational loss to BYU
top.description: LAHAINIA, HI- NOVEMBER 23: Tayshawn Comer #12 of the Washington Huskies goes to the basket over Nate Pickens #2 of the BYU Cougars in the first half during a first round Southwest Maui Invitational college basketball game at the Lahaina Civic Center on November 23, 2026 in Lahaina, Hawaii. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Though its coaching staff would likely roll their eyes at the mention of it, a moral victory was achieved in Washington’s 83-77 loss to #19 BYU in the opening round of the Maui Invitational. Given the trajectory of the two programs, a blowout loss suffered by the Huskies wouldn’t have been a surprise. For most, it was the expectation. Instead, UW looked the best it has under third year head coach Danny Sprinkle. Washington flew to Hawaii with an unbeaten record to its name. Victories over Colgate, Mississippi Valley State, Simon Fraser and Utah Tech are not enough to gloat, but victories are victories nonetheless. To go from those four opponents, to facing a nationally ranked foe is a significant leap, yet the Dawgs handled it well. Washington built a double digit lead within the first 10 minutes of the game. The hot start was especially impressive given UW wasn’t knocking down a bevy of three pointers. The Huskies were simply outplaying the Cougars and forced them out of their comfort zone. Eventually BYU returned the favor. Momentum shifted significantly in the second half when BYU’s full court press disrupted UW’s offensive flow. As UW’s scoring slowed, BYU’s opened up. After a first half that saw Washington outscore BYU 39-31, the Cougars outscored the Huskies 52-38 the rest of the way. Washington received its biggest scoring contributions from LeJuan Watts, who had 21 points off the bench and Ryan Beasley, who added 20. Lathan Sommerville was busy in the paint and added 13 points along with nine rebounds. Washington is back in action tomorrow against Clemson. top.description: ‘You Can’t Have a Game Like This’ — Former NFL LB ‘Concerned’ About Trevor Lawrence After Jaguars QB’s Struggles vs. Giants Trevor Lawrence had a rough afternoon in the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 23-18 Week 11 loss to the New York Giants, and it brought back memories of the quarterback fans thought they had moved on from. Lawrence completed 25 of 47 passes for 301 yards, one touchdown and two costly interceptions, ending the Jaguars’ three-game winning streak. Routine throws went missing, and Jacksonville managed just one touchdown on six trips inside the red zone. Former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho saw the same thing. He said this version of Lawrence reminded him of the old one, and that is a concern even with the Jaguars sitting at 7-3. Emmanuel Acho Worried by Trevor Lawrence’s Week 11 Struggles Speaking on the “Speakeasy” podcast Monday, Acho said every quarterback is allowed a bad game, but it was the way Lawrence threw his interceptions that bothered him. In Acho’s view, a team with real Super Bowl hopes can’t afford to give the ball away like that. “This game just worried me because it was flashbacks of old Trevor,” Acho said . “Everybody’s afforded a bad game. But in order to get where the Jags want to go, ’cause it’s fair to have Super Bowl expectations and conversations, Trevor, you can’t have a game like this. It would be one thing if Trevor’s interceptions were, like, tipped-ball interceptions or through-the-receiver’s-hands interceptions.” The former linebacker said the picks weren’t flukes, and he worried about what could happen if they showed up in the playoffs. top.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Sung-Mun Song #24 of the San Diego Padres leads off second base during the third inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Sung-Mun Song When Song played in Korea, he was an absolute star. In MLB, not so much. In his final season in the KBO, Song slashed .315/.387/.530 with 26 home runs. It was an incredible year. Because of that production, the Padres decided to sign him to a four-year, $15 million deal. At the time, Song was one of the most coveted international free agents. He’s yet to make good on that pedigree. Overall Grade: D Spring Training went well enough. Song posted a .235/.381/.412 slash line in eight Cactus League games. However, his spring was cut short when he suffered an oblique strain that kept him off of the Opening Day roster. He worked his way back from the injury and began the season in Triple-A. He was solid there (.655 OPS), and cracked the big-league roster in late April. Song struggled to acclimate to the big leagues in his first year. He was relegated to a bench player, though the infielder’s bat struggled even in those limited instances. The infielder hit .191/.291/.244 in 78 games (131 at-bats) with the Padres. nigeria.title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks. Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN. According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027. He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation. The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious. He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine. Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026. On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres. He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. nigeria.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. What I can’t understand is how are you trying to rob somebody and you don’t take her phone, nothing?” he said. Salami moved to the United States from France in 2024 after completing college and following her marriage. She is survived by her husband and their 4-year-old son, who lives with her mother in Togo. Chicago police have not publicly explained how the shootings were connected and no suspects have been identified. The fatal shooting has sparked calls for justice from her family, friends and members of the Togolese community in the U.S. Vanguard News The post Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school appeared first on Vanguard News .

business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. If you have been singing along to “ Feel Alright ” since E-Mortal Boy came out, Rema has just dropped the official lyric video so you can finally catch every single line without guessing. Having the words on screen makes it much easier to follow how Rema and Wizkid trade verses on the opening track, mixing smooth R&B-leaning melodies with English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba slang as they serenade a love interest. For plenty of listeners, “Feel Alright” is the biggest talking point on E-Mortal Boy because it marks the very first official collaboration between Rema and Wizkid, bringing two distinct Afrobeats eras together right at the start of the project. Putting out a lyric video for the track gives fans of both artists a chance to properly take in the lyrics and harmonies that have had the song on heavy rotation since the project landed. The release also keeps the spotlight on E-Mortal Boy, Rema’s seven-track EP that followed earlier singles “TEA” and “Oh No”. Alongside “Feel Alright” with Wizkid, the project includes “Velvet”, “TANZANIA” with BNYX, “SUGA” with Theodora , and closer “Bang Bang” with London and Kah-Lo , showing off the wide range of sounds Rema pulls together across the seven songs. If you have been waiting to learn every word of Rema and Wizkid’s first joint record, this lyric video has you covered. entertainment.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. Between beach days, the bustling Central Market in Port Louis, the lush trails of Black River Gorges National Park, and Casela Nature Parks keep a week-long itinerary full without ever feeling hectic. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.title: International Men’s Day: Six Films That Explore the Vulnerable Side of Men
entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Where does responsibility begin, and where does it end? Do men matter? Do their feelings matter? The theme for this year’s International Men’s Day is “The Future Is For Everyone.” For that, here are some movies that explore and illuminate the complexities of masculinity: The Pursuit of Happyness This classic film reveals the vulnerability often hidden behind male perseverance. Will Smith ’s portrayal of Chris Gardner challenges the stoic notion of manhood by showing fatherhood as both an act of love and endurance. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. Through this film, Kevin Hart shares his vision of what it means to be a man and a father. The gathering brought together some of Nigeria’s leading content creators, filmmakers, advertising professionals and brand executives to explore how digital influence can translate into original intellectual property, sustainable creative businesses and longer-term commercial opportunities. entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. You can be gracious and still be clear about the value you bring,” she added. The summit featured a distinguished line-up of women shaping leadership, business, finance, entertainment and corporate governance. entertainment.title: Inside the 2026 WIEN Gala & Awards: A Night of Celebration, Powerful Conversations and a New DEI Benchmark
entertainment.description: The Metropolitan Club, Lagos, was transformed into a gathering of some of the most influential names in Nigeria’s energy industry as the Women in Energy Network (WIEN) hosted its 2026 Gala & Awards. Bringing together industry leaders, policymakers, corporate executives and other distinguished guests, the evening marked six years of WIEN’s advocacy for greater representation, inclusion and leadership opportunities for women across the energy value chain. Beyond the glamour, elegant conversations and celebrations, the event carried a clear message: it is time to move beyond conversations about inclusion and focus on measurable progress. The Honourable Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Hajia Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim , delivered the special address, ably represented by Dr Adedayo Benjamins-Laniyi , Director-General/Chief Executive Officer of the Maryam Babangida National Centre for Women Development . In her address, WIEN President Eyono Fatayi-Williams emphasised that progress must be visible, measurable and sustained. “As we celebrate six years, we also have to ask ourselves an important question: What do the next six years look like? Because we cannot spend the next six years having the same conversations we have had in the last six years. We cannot continue to talk about inclusion without asking what has changed,” Fatayi-Williams challenged the industry. The evening also featured a keynote address by Dr Mutiu Sunmonu (CON) , Chairman of The Sage Centre for Leadership Excellence, who shared perspectives on leadership and the importance of creating opportunities for women to contribute meaningfully to the sector. sports.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis ahead of Joshua clash
sports.description: Tyson Fury will face British heavyweight rival Anthony Joshua in Cardiff next month (Chanakarn LAOSARAKHAM) Tyson Fury has said he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," said the heavyweight boxer. "It was like a living version of the pits of hell. "I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much. "The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that's when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London." Fury has made the revelations about his mental health in a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday. The 38-year-old is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua, a fellow former world champion, in Cardiff on December 11 -- a bout that will be broadcast live on Netflix. Fury recalled hearing the radio talking to him, and begging wife Paris to get him out of the hospital because "the Illuminati" wanted him. Following his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with alcohol and drug addiction. "It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind," he said. "I wouldn't be able to sit and have a conversation because I'd be hearing stuff in my mind. "I didn't know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again." After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed. Fury said a turning point in his life came when he was on a night out for Halloween in 2017. "I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, 'I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I'm a fat mess addicted to alcohol'," he said. But Fury added he channelled his disgust into a comeback which led him to return to training, focus more on his family and claim another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020. jdg/nf

sports.title: USA joint bid and UK confirmed as 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cup hosts
sports.description: FIFA announced Monday that the USA will co-host the 2031 Women's World Cup with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica, while the UK will host in 2035 (OZAN KOSE) FIFA on Monday confirmed that a joint bid led by the United States will host the expanded, 48-team Women's World Cup in 2031, while the United Kingdom will host the following edition in 2035. The winning bids were waved through by acclamation after FIFA president Gianni Infantino confirmed the USA in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time. The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035. Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at a virtual gathering of FIFA's member associations. "As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years." The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final. The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams. The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times. - 'Landmark moment' - US Soccer reacted to the announcement by saying the awarding of the 2031 tournament gave the country the chance to "build on the momentum" of this year's World Cup as well as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The United States are the reigning Olympic women's football champions. No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. A joint statement by the four UK national associations described the announcement as "a landmark moment". It is not yet known which cities will host matches at the respective tournaments, but most matches in 2031 are likely to take place in the United States while England can expect to have the lion's share of venues in 2035. The UK bid proposed 22 stadiums in total, with 16 in England, three in Wales, two in Scotland and one in Northern Ireland. Lawrence completed 25 of 47 passes for 301 yards, one touchdown and two costly interceptions, ending the Jaguars’ three-game winning streak. Routine throws went missing, and Jacksonville managed just one touchdown on six trips inside the red zone. Former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho saw the same thing. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Sung-Mun Song When Song played in Korea, he was an absolute star. In MLB, not so much. In his final season in the KBO, Song slashed .315/.387/.530 with 26 home runs. It was an incredible year. Because of that production, the Padres decided to sign him to a four-year, $15 million deal. At the time, Song was one of the most coveted international free agents. He’s yet to make good on that pedigree. Overall Grade: D Spring Training went well enough. Song posted a .235/.381/.412 slash line in eight Cactus League games. However, his spring was cut short when he suffered an oblique strain that kept him off of the Opening Day roster. He worked his way back from the injury and began the season in Triple-A. He was solid there (.655 OPS), and cracked the big-league roster in late April. Song struggled to acclimate to the big leagues in his first year. technology.description: Don't mind the recent arrests. The ShinyHunters extortion gang may still be operating, just under the new name of Inception, according to Okta's threat intelligence group. ShinyHunters is the brash cybercriminal group that, most recently, breached rival gang Clop before hacking the FBI , resulting in at least three arrests of key suspects in September and October. The crims - and their old data leak site - have since gone dark. “While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion,” Okta threat hunters Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said on Monday. Okta tracks this threat cluster as O-UNC-053 - the “O-UNC” prefix stands for an Okta Uncategorized cluster, and it uses this label before formally attributing the activity to a named threat group. While Okta hasn't formally confirmed O-UNC-053 to be the same crime crew as ShinyHunters, the identity and access management provider’s researchers note that it does use nearly identical social engineering tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Plus, they note: O-UNC-053 operators change the themes of their phishing domains about every four to six weeks, and they also post claimed victims on ShinyHunters’ data leak site. In November, however, organizations targeted by O-UNC-053 began appearing on a new data leak site branded as Inception and not ShinyHunters. The first five - Advanced Micro Devices, Cigna Healthcare, Paychex, PepsiCo, and Henry Schein - appeared November 17 on the site, and all were marked “leaked.” Soon after, security maven Dominic Alvieri questioned if Inception was linked to ShinyHunters. “ShinyHunters are not all in jail,” he wrote on social media. On November 19, AutoZone appeared on the site, with Inception again claiming to have leaked the auto-parts retailer's files. On Saturday, EV technology firm Lucid Group joined the claimed victims. None of the seven companies have confirmed breaches, and none responded to The Register ’s inquiries. We will update this story when we receive more information. Okta Threat Intelligence “is unable to validate if published data is authentic,” the researchers said in response to our questions. In the Monday report, the Okta team does note that Inception’s new data leak site listings “included multiple targets for which Okta Threat Intelligence previously observed O-UNC-053 infrastructure registration.” The infrastructure was registered between six and 19 days before Inception listed the companies on its leak site, and this gap “is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” Diallo and Nickels added. technology.title: Amazon scoops up AI accelerator tech to keep chips busy at all times
technology.description: Amazon has agreed to buy AI optimization technology from an Israeli startup in a bid to speed up its inference operations. The house of Bezos on Monday announced a deal to purchase proprietary AI acceleration tech from Decart AI, known as the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), for an undisclosed amount. Amazon also plans to bring Decart’s three founders and their engineering team into the fold. Decart’s DOS is designed to push AI hardware closer to its maximum performance across different AI models and hardware platforms. The company claims that most AI chips live their lives without reaching their full potential – practically a sin in this age of increased hardware costs and limited availability – and DOS aims to fix that by operating between the model and the chip, optimizing kernels, compilers, and runtimes for the underlying hardware “so every core stays busy.” DOS is hardware-agnostic, with Decart saying it supports Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, and, most critically for our purposes here, AWS Trainium chips. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost,” Peter DeSantis, Amazon SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, and quantum computing, said in the announcement. “That's the pillar Trainium and our AI efforts are built on, and from our earliest work with Decart, we knew they … would help us push it even further.” Decart doesn’t offer much in the way of details about its proprietary AI-maxxing tech, but claims it can reduce latency, improve throughput, and reduce the costs associated with training and inference runs. An Amazon spokesperson clarified to The Register that the deal is an asset purchase and not a full company acquisition, with Amazon only acquiring DOS and the tech behind it as well as personnel. As for what may become of Decart after the deal, that’s unclear. Amazon told us to reach out to Decart to learn what may happen to any remaining employees and the company’s other technology, but we didn’t hear back. Along with offering its optimization stack, Decart has a couple of different AI models: Lucy, a live video model marketed toward advertisers, live streamers, and the like; and Oasis, a world model AI marketed toward companies working on embodied AI applications. Decart’s non-DOS assets weren’t mentioned in the press release, and per the Amazon spokesperson we talked to, that means they weren’t part of the deal. We can’t imagine that the Decart team is too upset about the potential abandonment of those models, though: While neither company has disclosed a price, Bloomberg claims its sources value the deal at around $7.5 billion. If Bloomberg's figure is accurate, that would make this deal one of the most expensive in Amazon’s history, right between its $3.9 billion acquisition of One Medical and its $8.5 billion purchase of film studio MGM . ®

science.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal. "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer, associate professor at OSU's Department of Botany and Plant Pathology, said in a statement . "That's an important step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the moon." To grow the spuds, the scientists used five different materials that are similar to regolith , the dust and rocks that cover the moon's surface. The moon contains various regions with unique surface makeups, so the materials they used simulated regolith from both lunar mare and lunar highland regions. The secret ingredient was vermicompost, a soil that's rich in nutrients. The team added different levels of vermicompost to the simulated regolith to grow the potatoes. They figured out that fake regolith mixed with 30 percent vermicompost worked about as well as growing potatoes with regular soil. Oregon State University researchers David Handy and Aymeric Goyer studying potatoes grown in lunar regolith. (Image credit: Aymeric Goyer/David Handy/OSU) "We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith by reducing plant exposure to harmful compounds," David Handy, a postdoctoral researcher in Goyer's lab, said in the same statement. The idea is that astronauts in the future could bring a little nutrient-rich soil with them and mix it with regolith to grow potatoes. After all, it'd cost a ton to ship all that food from Earth. NASA funding supported this research.

science.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
science.description: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, is managing the acquisition, and NOAA will own and operate the instruments and deliver the data to users worldwide. Microwave sounders provide critical measurements of temperature and moisture in the atmosphere, which significantly influence weather patterns. The SMBA instruments could improve the medium-range forecasts for NOAA’s National Weather Service. The NEON mission is a collaboration between NASA and NOAA. The mission is led by NOAA, which provides funding, technical requirements, and postlaunch operations. NASA will manage the development of the NEON satellites and launch them for NOAA. NASA and NOAA will work with commercial partners to design and build the NEON spacecraft and instruments. science.title: How sci‑fi imagines sports in microgravity, and how zero‑g sports might actually work
science.description:
Alan Bradley is an experienced tech and culture writer with more than 20 years covering gaming, tech, and hardware. He has served as commerce director and in senior editorial roles at major publications. His work has appeared in Rolling Stone, U.S. News & World Report, PCMag, TechRadar, GamesRadar+, CNET, Live Science, Variety, and many other outlets. Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. It defines how balls arc, how quickly players can move, and even how we orient ourselves in play spaces. Remove the gravity, and all of those assumptions and mechanics evaporate as well. "First of all, in zero g, Isaac Newton will win every time," Les Johnson, former Chief Technologist for NASA, told Space. Les is a physicist with over 35 years of experience working at Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, as well as a science fiction author. "'For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,'" quotes Johnson. "This is very difficult to simulate in real life due to gravity; special effects often try to compensate. With today’s AI and green screens, it can actually look good on screen." In a microgravity scenario, the concept of up and down is no longer relevant. Suddenly, the playing field expands from a single, fixed plane to a fully three-dimensional space that includes height. (Image credit: Netflix) Momentum is also a completely different beast. Instead of being able to quickly stop and pivot the way you can during terrestrial sports, once you start moving in microgravity, you keep going until something stops you. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
science.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history?
